source.title: Population morphology implies a common developmental blueprint for Drosophila motion detectors

method_boundary.observation: The published method states that correct rooting of each neuron at the soma is manually verified and corrected when needed.
method_boundary.consequence: The root of the input tree itself may differ from an unreviewed skeleton root; root identity must therefore be treated as a separately reviewed property.

method_boundary.observation: After correct soma rooting, the published method identifies a branch node by a tree-structure metric that maximises terminal leaves while minimising subtree cable weight.

The publication then performs a second manual verification of all neurons to ensure the selected subtree is the complete dendrite, with individual routing/skeletonization errors correctable through the GUI.
method_boundary.consequence: Matching the automated subtree-selection root does not prove that two final morphology artifacts are topologically or metrically identical.

method_boundary.observation: The publication separately describes global alignment of dendrite populations using mean-centering, eigendecomposition, fitted-sphere centering, and axis/orientation rotations.
method_boundary.consequence: Global spatial alignment is a downstream coordinate operation and must not be silently assumed to be the transform used for the December 2025 Point_data artifact.

method_boundary.observation: The publication separately describes individual eigendecomposition/PCA alignment and explicit scaling for overlay/shape analysis.
method_boundary.consequence: These operations are distinct from root review, subtree selection, manual morphology correction, and raw tree identity.

relation_to_project.observed: The project reproduces the published automated subtree-selection decision on the four committed SWCs, but historical Point_data morphology metrics disagree for three of the four anchors at segment/node/leaf/cable levels.
relation_to_project.interpretation: The published method now establishes two manual morphology review boundaries around the automated extraction: soma-root verification occurs before the tree-structure selection, and a second review can modify the selected dendritic compartment and correct individual errors. This is a documented possible explanation for morphology disagreement, but no historical per-neuron edit record or December 2025 producer artifact has been recovered.
